name: Mullet
summary: A cut with a shorter front and sides and a distinctly longer back at the neckline.
intro: The shape is easiest to read in profile. The ear and temple sit inside a compact side section while the rear hair continues down the neck.
The contrast can be sharp or softly blended. A wolf cut relies more on layering through the crown and face, whereas a mullet is defined by the length left at the back.
The cut became prominent in Australian popular culture in the 1970s and 1980s.

variations.name: Classic mullet
variations.description: A short front and open sides frame a long back that extends down the neck.

variations.name: Curly mullet
variations.description: Keeps curl length at the nape and uses a shorter front and sides to expose the contrast.

variations.name: Short mullet
variations.description: Retains a modest step in length toward the neckline, with a softer outline.

consultation.intro: Bring a side-view reference and agree on the longest point and how much hair to remove around the ears.
questions: Where should the rear lengths end when dry?
How much of the ear should the sides expose?
Should the side-to-back transition be sharp or blended?
consultation.sampleRequest: “Keep the longest hair at the nape, make the sides noticeably shorter, and leave enough length at the front for a short textured fringe.”

considerations: Check the profile as well as the front. The front can look like a crop even when the back has substantial length.
Allow for curl shrinkage when setting the dry length at the nape.
